definitions.explanation: A man who is getting married or has just married.
The husband of one's daughter. Also used for a man who marries into and takes his wife's family name.

examples.japanese: ⟦{花嫁|はなよめ}→花嫁：04318_hanayome⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{婿|むこ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入場|にゅうじょう}→入場：03521_nyuujou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{婿|むこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}している→探す：00493_sagasu⟧。
examples.english: I'm looking for a husband for my daughter.

examples.japanese: ⟦{立派|りっぱ}→立派：01093_rippa⟧な{婿|むこ}さんです⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: What a fine son-in-law you have.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{婿養子|むこようし}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧{田中家|たなかけ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: He married into the Tanaka family as an adopted son-in-law.

examples.japanese: うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{婿|むこ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{気|き}が{利|き}く→気が利く：06880_kigakiku⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧だ。
examples.english: Our son-in-law is a very considerate person.

examples.japanese: ⟦{跡取|あとと}り→跡取り：14280_atotori⟧がいない⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{婿|むこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ことにした。
examples.english: Since there was no heir, they decided to take in a son-in-law.

notes:
USAGE:
When referring to someone else's son-in-law or groom politely, お{婿|むこ}さん is used. {婿養子|むこようし} specifically refers to a man who marries into his wife's family and takes her surname — a practice with deep roots in Japanese family law and tradition.

The expression {婿|むこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ means to take in a son-in-law (i.e., to have a man marry into the family).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{花|はな}{婿|むこ}→花婿：21346_hanamuko⟧: bridegroom (formal)
- {婿養子|むこようし}: adopted son-in-law
- {婿|むこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to take in a son-in-law
- {婿入|むこい}り: marrying into the wife's family
